title: Same answer, same verdict
statement: Make every verdict reproducible: judge at the most deterministic setting and freeze or cache each machine judgment, so the same input always gets the same verdict.
detail: In a reading lesson's review round, an identical typed answer was re-judged to a different verdict on resubmit. The fix ran the first judging attempt at the most deterministic model setting and cached identical resubmits so they return the same verdict at once. Freeze each machine judgment with its evidence before the pass-or-fail gate runs, so the same input, a resubmitted answer included, always gets the same verdict.
against: The standard sits in a staged proposal, and nothing cited here shows its gate in use (`grade3-reading/knowledge_bot/pr-proposals/ti-courseplans-standards/staged/docs/standards/README.md`).

Same `course_id` + same `COMPLIANCE.md` + same referenced artifacts → same verdict and exit code. No model calls in the gate path; any machine-judged input must already be frozen into the ledger with its evidence tag before the gate runs.
**Exit code:** `0` iff every required row is `PASS` (`all_green == true`); non-zero otherwise. This is the CI-gateable signal.

Each scoped owner now maps a judged, trimmed exact answer to its original settled turn ID.
A different result the second time is a scorer bug, not the child's fault.
Current lastScoredRef forgets A and makes a third judged request, allowing contradictory verdict or premature floor.

**The same answer must earn the same verdict.** An open-response scorer that returns "Almost" and then accepts the identical word on resubmission teaches a child that grading is a slot machine. Judgment retries must not resample at a different temperature; only PARSE failures may re-ask, and a scored verdict for identical answer text within an attempt session should be sticky.
(Compounding is LLM/stochastic — not byte-reproducible like the deterministic gates below.)
